summary: Temporary org-scoped audit role for SecOps to access legacy cloud projects
description:
Issue summary: SecOps requests temporary org-scoped audit access to investigate suspected misconfiguration in legacy projects. Impact: Without read-only org-level visibility, SecOps cannot complete an audit of IAM bindings and org policies across several legacy accounts that predate centralized org policies. This blocks a security ticket and delaying a compliance audit scheduled for next week.

Request: Grant a time-bound, read-only audit role for two SecOps engineers (names below) with explicit permission boundary and session duration = 8 hours, renewable once pending justification. Scope must include: list org policy viewing, IAM role bindings read, project/folder metadata, CloudTrail/S3 bucket metadata read for AWS accounts, and equivalent GCP Organization Viewer on listed legacy projects.

Justification: Legacy projects (tagged legacy:true) were created before the consolidated org structure. SecOps needs consolidated visibility to confirm no overly broad roles or unmanaged service accounts exist. This is strictly investigative (no write).

Requested principals:
- secops.lead@redwood.com (Maya Patel)
- secops.senior@redwood.com (Daniel Ortiz)

Proposed temporary identities and permissions:
- AWS: Create role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodTempOrgAudit-INT-423004 with trust limited to SAML/Okta and MFA enforced. Attach managed policy Redwood/OrgAuditReadOnly and permission boundary arn:aws:iam::123456789012:policy/Redwood/Boundaries/ReadOnlyAudit.
- GCP: Create service account redwood-secops-temp@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com with roles/resourcemanager.organizationViewer, roles/browser and an IAM condition restricting to projects with label legacy=true.

Duration & controls: 8-hour sessions, max 16 hours total (renewable after review). All sessions must be logged, must use Bastion/session manager in AWS with recording enabled, and SECOPS must run actions through an approved ephemeral auth flow (Okta then STS/GCP IAM).

Audit requirements: Export CloudTrail, stackdriver logs, and session recordings to the security audit bucket; enable object-level logging for any S3 buckets accessed. Provide a post-access audit report with steps taken, queries run, and any credentials discovered.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Role/SA provisioned and validated in test account; 2) SecOps can list org-level IAM bindings and view projects labeled legacy; 3) Access expires as expected and audit artifacts are present.

Steps to reproduce: N/A (access request).
comments: Maya Patel (2026-02-20): Filing this request on behalf of SecOps. We need to complete a sweep of legacy projects before the vendor audit next Thursday. Prefer minimal scope and strong controls.
Rajiv Menon (2026-02-20): Acknowledged. Will review required permissions and propose a role template by EOD tomorrow. Need confirmation of exact legacy project IDs and the GCP org id.

Daniel Ortiz (2026-02-21): Provided project list in Slack #secops: proj-legacy-01, proj-legacy-02, proj-legacy-eu. GCP org: redwood-prod-org. Also noted a previous PR that created an org viewer policy (see infra PR).

Rajiv Menon (2026-02-22): Drafted role/policy template in infra repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1287. Waiting on IAM review and okta trust config. Marking blocked on IAM policy verification.

Linh Zhao (IAM team) (2026-02-24): Verified proposed permission boundary and read-only policy. Requesting that we restrict S3 object read to buckets prefixed with 'audit-' and add SLA tag on the role for expiration enforcement.
investigation_notes: Confirmed legacy tag pattern using inventory query: gcloud projects list --filter='labels.legacy:true' returned 3 projects and aws resource groups tagged legacy:true returned 5 accounts.
Checked previous org roles: roles/OrganizationAuditViewer does not exist; we will create a scoped role 'RedwoodTempOrgAudit-INT-423004' with no write permissions.
Validated that CloudTrail in three AWS accounts is delivering to security-audit bucket: s3://redwood-security-audit-prod. Need to ensure S3 GET events are logged (enable Data Events).
Ran dry-run of proposed policy against simulatePrincipalPolicy in AWS for the example ARN and confirmed only List and Get-like actions are allowed (no Put/Delete).
Noted GCP IAM condition syntax to restrict to projects with label legacy=true: using 'resource.matchLabels("legacy","true")' in binding condition per runbook.

Identified required follow-ups: 1) Okta SAML trust config for role; 2) Automation to enforce session expiration (Lambda for AWS STS and Security Command Center for GCP); 3) Create short-lived audit bucket path for session recordings.
resolution:
Provisioned time-bound audit identities and documented controls. Actions taken: 1) Created AWS role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodTempOrgAudit-INT-423004 with managed policy Redwood/OrgAuditReadOnly and permission boundary Redwood/Boundaries/ReadOnlyAudit. 2) Configured Okta SAML app with role mapping, MFA required. 3) Created GCP service account redwood-secops-temp@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com and bound roles/resourcemanager.organizationViewer + roles/browser with an IAM condition limiting to legacy projects. 4) Enabled CloudTrail data event logging for the audit bucket and configured session-manager recording; session access tested by Maya on 2026-02-24.

Post-access controls: Role set to auto-disable after 16 hours; actions logged to s3://redwood-security-audit-prod/INT-423004/. PR merging infra changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1287.

Follow-ups: Create automation ticket to add an expiration enforcement Lambda and add this pattern to the Cloud Access Runbook. Recommend scheduling a short blameless review with SecOps after audit completion.
